# narrative-strategist insight

Career-transition articles are strongest when the resume is treated as a purpose-built signal whose emphasis must change with the target role. Humor can name the friction once, but executive credibility comes from owning the recalibration and separating transferable evidence from requirements still to be proven.

Direct technical tutorials should state the finished architecture and build order before the detailed explanation. Move from idea to sequence to source files to runtime path to proof. Embedded visuals should show the real implementation and rendered result, so they function as evidence for the prose instead of as a separate conceptual detour.

Workflow articles should foreground the configured operating system when that system performs the implementation. Start with the human request, distinguish standing roles from the request-specific run graph, show build and independent acceptance ownership, and make the final human approval boundary explicit. Implementation mechanics can support the explanation, but they should not replace the workflow the author actually uses.
